title: Replying on a mailbox before acknowledging its page takes five calls (read, send, ack, re-read own send, ack); document or provide a lower-friction sanctioned protocol
outcome: An agent that replies on a mailbox while processing a page can complete that exchange in fewer calls, or the five-call sequence is documented as the sanctioned protocol with its reason, keeping the current durable acknowledgement semantics. Reported by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #118, 2026-10-01 05:34Z), first observed in CV2 session-9302 at 05:33Z: replying before acknowledging a page requires read, send, acknowledge, re-read own send, acknowledge (five calls); later sends advance the cursor automatically only when the cursor already sits directly before the new message. Directions: let an acknowledgement with a receipt also cover the sender's own messages appended after the page, or let send accept the page receipt and acknowledge it atomically; or document the sequence in the mailbox tool descriptions.
acceptance: An agent that reads a page, replies on the same mailbox and then acknowledges the page ends with its cursor past its own reply without a second read, or the tool descriptions document the required sequence and why; a test covers the chosen behaviour.
Durable acknowledgement semantics are unchanged: no unread inbound message is ever skipped; a test covers an inbound message arriving between the read and the reply.
